item.title: Target faces renewed backlash for Halloween costume with 'minstrel show features'
item.description: Retailer Target pulled a children's Halloween costume from its shelves after widespread social media backlash, apologizing for selling a garment critics said evoked racist minstrel caricatures.
item.content:encoded:
Retailer Target pulled a children's Halloween costume from its shelves after widespread social media backlash, apologizing for selling a garment critics said evoked racist minstrel caricatures.

(Image credit: Charles Krupa)

item.title: Mexican cattle allowed in the U.S. after a yearlong ban
item.description: A border crossing in Arizona opened to cattle from Mexico for the first time in more than a year. This despite a parasite being found on the Mexican side. U.S. ranchers are upset.
item.content:encoded: A border crossing in Arizona opened to cattle from Mexico for the first time in more than a year. This despite a parasite being found on the Mexican side. U.S. ranchers are upset.

item.title: Colorado resort town suing ICE's landlord over detentions
item.description: A city in Colorado is suing the landlord of an ICE processing facility there, saying its detentions there violate local zoning codes.

item.title: Trump administration unveils new Iran sanctions
item.description: The Trump administration has struggled to find an exit ramp to the war against Iran. Now, it is trying to step up the financial pressure instead by introducing new sanctions to end the six month war.

item.title: Spokane wildfire evacuees return home, but it's 'still a hazmat situation'
item.description: Most evacuees have been allowed to return to their homes near burn zones in Spokane, despite concerns about lingering toxins.

item.title: Churches, libraries and breweries: Inside DHS' covert surveillance operation
item.description: DHS allegedly went undercover at community meetings, subpoenaed the financial records of labor unions, and created dossiers on people at a church gathering, according to court filings.

item.title: When is suspending students discrimination? Education Department renews an old fight
item.description: President Trump's Education Department is telling schools to stop considering race when it comes to school discipline.

item.title: At least 25% of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE, study finds
item.description: Playing football has long been linked to the brain disease known as CTE, but how prevalent it is is still unknown. A new study of former NFL players who died recently found that at least 25% had CTE.

item.title: 30 structures burned in Reno's Hawk Fire, officials say
item.description: Officials have confirmed more than 30 structures have burned in the Hawk Fire just northwest of Reno, Nevada.
